text:
Livspace, Licious, Moglix, Country Delight. All backed by investors sitting in Singapore.

Most Indian founders only pitch Indian VCs. But Singapore-based funds have been writing cheques into Indian startups for years, from ₹4 Cr pre-seed bets to growth-stage debt.

In this carousel: 8 Singapore investors that back Indian founders, with their stage, cheque size, Indian portfolio and how to reach each one.

Quick tip: match the investor to your stage before you pitch. Antler and BEENEXT write early cheques, Jungle and Vertex lead seed to Series A rounds, while Venturi, EvolutionX and Temasek come in much later.

Save this for your next raise.

carousel.title: 8 Singapore investors that back Indian founders
carousel.subtitle: From pre-seed cheques to growth debt: stage, cheque size, Indian portfolio and how to reach each one.

investors.name: Antler
investors.reach: antler.co/india — pitch directly via Antler Direct
investors.note: Backs founders at day zero, even before a product exists.

investors.name: BEENEXT
investors.note: India is its biggest market by number of portfolio companies.

investors.name: Jungle Ventures
investors.note: India is now its largest market, at nearly 70% of capital deployed.

investors.name: Vertex Ventures SEA & India
investors.stage: Seed to Series B (mostly Series A)
investors.note: Backs 6–9 startups a year, so come with clear Series A metrics.

investors.name: Qualgro
investors.note: Mainly a Southeast Asia investor; India deals are selective, so a global or SEA angle helps.

investors.name: Venturi Partners
investors.reach: Via its website or a warm intro
investors.note: Growth stage only; bookmark it for after your Series A.

investors.name: EvolutionX Debt Capital
investors.cheque: Large debt deals (e.g. ₹287.5 Cr to upGrad)
investors.note: Non-dilutive capital for scaled companies, not for early stage.

investors.name: Temasek
investors.cheque: Large; early stage is ~5% of portfolio
investors.note: Also backs Indian VC funds, so it can reach you indirectly earlier.
